sentences.text:
Ramesh vs The State Of M.P. on 14 August, 2024
 Neutral Citation No. 2024:Mphc-Ind:23385
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi

On The 14th Of August, 2024
 Criminal Appeal No. 230 of 2001
 Ramesh
 Versus
 The State Of M.P.
 Appearance:
 Shri Jitendra Bajpai - Advocate for appellant.

Shri Rajesh Joshi - Govt. Advocate for the respondent /
 Order

This appeal is directed against the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence dated 09/02/2001 passed by Special Sessions Judge, West Nimar, Mandleshwar (M.P.) in Sessions Trial No.377/2000, whereby acquitting the appellant / accused under Section 304-B and 306 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred as, 'IPC') and appellant Ramesh, who is husband of deceased Devka Bai, has been convicted for the offence under Section 498-A of IPC and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment of 02 years with fine of Rs.2,000/- with default stipulation.

entities.text: Special Sessions Judge, West Nimar, Mandleshwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. It is undisputed that Devka Bai was married to the appellant.
It is also undisputed that Devka Bai has died on 05/06/2000 under suspicious circumstances by consuming some poisonous substance.
The facts as having emerged from the FIR are that marriage of Devka Bai was solemnized with the appellant Ramesh near about three to four years prior to her death.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23385 2 CRA-230-2001 3.

In the earlier part of marriage she was living peacefully with the appellant and his relatives, but on death of new born baby boy of Devka Bai, appellant and her in-laws started meting out cruelty to the deceased.
The appellant off and on physically assaulting her after consuming liquor.
Being subdued to the cruelty meted out to the deceased, she consumed some poisonous substance and died.
4. On an information a merg under Section 174 of Cr.P.C. was registered and inquired into.
After recording the statement of witnesses, it was found that the deceased committed suicide due to the harassment given by the appellant and her in-laws.

After that an FIR at Crime No.189/2000 under Section 304(B)/34 of IPC was registered at Police Station Kasrawad, District Khargone and Ramesh vs The State Of M.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86189931/

sentences.text: investigation ensued.
During investigation, Resolution of Panchayat was seized and Seizure Memo (Ex.-P/9) was prepared.
After postmortem of body of the deceased, a sealed pack bottle of viscera was seized and seizure memo (Ex.-P/11) was prepared.
Viscera was sent for FSL examination vide memorandum of Superintendent of Police, Khargone dated 16/06/2000 (Ex.-P/12).

Statement of witnesses Tarasingh and others were recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. and after completion of the investigation, charge sheet was filed before the Court of competent local jurisdiction.
The Magistrate in turn committed the case to the Court of Sessions for trial.
5. Learned trial Court framed charges against the appellant and his mother Tarabai under Section 498-A, 304(B)/34 and 306 of IPC.
When the charges were read over to the appellant, he abjured the guilt.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23385 3 CRA-230-2001 6.
Prosecution to prove its case examined as many as nine witnesses and also marked documents (Ex.-P/1 to P/12).
The incriminating circumstances appearing in the prosecution witnesses were placed before the appellant while examining him under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
The appellant pleaded ignorance about most of the circumstances with further defence that he is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the matter.
There is no tradition of giving dowry in their society and opposite to this money is paid by the groom's side to the bride.
To prove his defence, appellant has examined Raju (DW-1) and Parasram (DW-2) that Devka Bai was never subjected to cruelty by the appellant or his relatives.

Learned trial Court vide impugned judgment acquitting the accused from the offences under Section 304(B) and 306 of IPC but convicted him for the offence under Section 498- A of IPC and sentenced him as mentioned herein above.
Hence, this appeal.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant drawing attention of this Court towards para 16 and 17 submitted that trial Court has recorded the finding that there was no harassment with regard to the demand of dowry and it has also been recognized by the trial Court that there is no tradition in the society of appellant and the deceased of demand of dowry.

Learned counsel further submits that serious infirmities and anomalies in the statement of prosecution witnesses have been ignored by the trial Court and judgment has been passed on conjectures and surmises for recording a finding that offence under Section 498-A of IPC has been proved.
On these grounds, learned counsel for the appellant prays for allowing appeal and setting aside conviction and sentence thereon.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23385 4 CRA-230-2001 8.
In alternative limb of prayer, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the alleged incident took place on 05/06/2000 near about more than 24 years back.
Appellant has no criminal antecedents.
He is facing prosecution for so many long years during trial and also in the appeal.
He further submits that from 19/06/2000 to 21/07/2000 near about 33 days the appellant was in jail as mentioned in para 28 of the impugned judgment.

On these contentions, he submits that if the offence against the appellant is found proved, even then the sentence may be reduced to the period already undergone by him and even by enhancing reasonable amount of fine.

To bolster his submission, learned counsel placed reliance on the judgment by the apex Court in the case of Suresh Ramesh vs The State Of M.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86189931/
2

sentences.text: 9. Sounding contra note, learned counsel for the State submits that the impugned judgment is based on due appreciation of evidence.
There is ample evidence to prove that deceased was subjected to cruelty by the appellant / husband which ultimately resulted in untimely death of Devka Bai.

For this, learned counsel inviting attention of this Court towards para 18 of the impugned judgment and also invited attention of this Court towards the statements of prosecution witnesses Tarasingh (PW-2), Narsingh (PW-3) and Rami (PW-4).
On these contentions, learned counsel submits that appeal being sans merits deserves to be dismissed.

10. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
11.
The evidence adduced in support of the allegation with regard to Section 498-A of IPC is found to be clear, cogent and consistent.
The same NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23385 5 CRA-230-2001 is free from any material infirmities.
Tarasingh (PW-2), brother of Devka Bai has stated before the trial Court that after the birth of new born son of deceased Dwarka Bai, appellant and his mother started harassing her.
Same has been corroborated by the statement of Narsingh (PW-3) and Rami (PW- 4).
The testimony of the prosecution witnesses stands duly corroborated by the FIR (Ex.-P/8).
Apart from the above oral evidence by Ex.-P/9 to P/10, deed with regard to resolution in Panchayat Ex.-P/3 and P/4 also proved the prosecution case.
In Ex.-P/3, it has been mentioned that in future Devka Bai will not be harassed.

12. In the impugned judgment in para 15, 16 and 17 of finding has been recorded that harassment with regard to demand of dowry is not proved but on the basis of evidence led in the case, learned Court below has recorded the finding of conviction under Section 498-A of IPC.

For ready reference,
provision as contained in Section 498-A of IPC is reproduced herein below:
"498A.
Husband
or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.--

Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

Explanation.--For the purposes of this section, "cruelty"
means-- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:23385 6 CRA-230-2001 with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."

Ramesh vs The State Of M.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86189931/
3

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From bare perusal of the above provision, it is apparent that if cruelty is meted out to the wife offence under Section 498-A of IPC is attracted irrespective of the fact whether cruelty has been committed for demand of dowry or for any other reason.
In view of the above arguments on behalf of counsel for the appellant that demand of dowry is not proved is of no consequence.

13. In the light of the aforesaid discussion, this Court is of the view that conviction of the appellant as recorded by learned trial Court vide impugned judgment does not suffers from any infirmity and is hereby affirmed.
14. As regards sentence, the prayer made on behalf of the appellant appears to be reasonable.
The incident took place on 05/06/2000 about 24 years back.
The appellant is facing trial for last 24 years.

No criminal antecedents are attributed to the appellant, therefore, period of jail sentence is reduced to the period already undergone by the appellant i.e. from 19/06/2000 to 21/07/2000 for 33 days in view of the judgment by Apex Court in the the case of Suresh Damu Mistry (Supra) .
15. Accordingly, this appeal is partly allowed and conviction of the appellant is affirmed by reducing the jail sentence to the period already undergone by him.
The appellant is on bail.
His bail bonds and personal bonds stand discharged.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23385 7 CRA-230-2001 16.
Let a copy of this judgment along with record be sent to the concerned trial Court for information and necessary compliance.
Certified copy as per rules.
